messages:
jen: heads-up — seeing a sharp uptick in Xid events in us-west2-gpu-pool around 01:05 UTC, mostly Xid 13 and 31. raising for triage :eyes:
kai: which codes exactly and any sample logs? 13 vs 31 have different root causes so want to scope before we start node-drain dance
jen: pasted quick grep from node-logs (small excerpt):
```
May 05 01:07:21 gpu-node-13 kernel: NVRM: Xid (13): 79, PID 24213: GPU has fallen off the bus.
May 05 01:07:21 gpu-node-13 kernel: NVRM: Xid (31): 13, Channel ID 00000005
May 05 01:07:45 gpu-node-13 nvidia-modeset: probe failed, pci error rx non-pci
```
kai: thanks. can you run the prometheus query for the last 3h to map by model and workload label? something like: 
```
sum by(code, model, job_label) (increase(nvidia_xid_total[3h]))
```
jеn: ran that. results (summarized): Xid13 -> 70 events, 80% from model_class=bert-infer-large, seq_len>512; Xid31 -> 23 events, distributed across retriever/embedding jobs. most Xid13s are on h100-48gb instances.
nate: that matches a pattern we saw last month — long prefix/prefill + continuous batching triggers memory map churn on H100s and occasionally trips Xid13. A100s tended to show 31 when PCIe resets happened.
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu_xid_rate{code="13",pool="us-west2-gpu-pool"} > 5m threshold — 01:08:17 UTC — see https://ops.redwood/alerts/7461
kai: good signal. next: check ECC volatile counters to rule out physical memory degradation. run: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `nvidia-smi --query-ecc=volatile,aggregate --format=csv` on affected GPUs. also collect dmesg + kernel oops snippets.
jen: quick ECC extract from one affected device: `Volatile ECC: 0, Aggregate ECC: 124` — the aggregate suggests historical soft errors but volatile is 0 at sample time.
nate: aggregate can be noisy; what's important is recurring increase over short windows. I recommend correlating `increase(nvidia_ecc_aggregate[1h])` with the xid spikes. If they track, hardware is suspect.
kai: also check driver/firmware versions. we recently rolled driver 535.86 on this pool? if so, there are known regressions causing GPU reset storms under heavy concurrent kernels.
jen: nodes report driver=535.86 and cuda=12.3. I can roll back a test node to 535.73 in staging.
sre-oncall: operational plan suggestion: 1) mitigate at software layer — reduce max_batch_tokens and disable continuous batching for bert-large routes; 2) add per-gpu xid-rate alert + per-gpu ECC-surge alert; 3) schedule a slow rolling driver rollback on a small subset to validate. avoid mass drain until we confirm hardware vs driver.
kai: for monitoring, add panels: per-GPU Xid rate heatmap, Xid-by-code histogram, model_class vs xid scatter, and a short-window flatten alert for >10 Xid13 in 10m on a single GPU. prometheus exprs: `increase(nvidia_xid_total{code="13"}[10m]) > 10` and `increase(nvidia_ecc_aggregate[15m]) > 50`
jen: I also pulled container level info — same pod image hash across failures, so less likely container bug. consistent runtime traffic pattern: long-prompt inference with large kv-cache prefill.
nate: mitigation that worked previously: force-prefill-to-streaming and cap prefill tokens per request or use the shorter prompt variant. also, add a graceful fallback model (smaller) for the canary rollout window.
sre-oncall: hardware triage if driver rollback doesn't help: 1) power-cycle PCIe slot and reseat card; 2) run vendor diag (`nvidia-diag` / NVPM tests); 3) if persistent Xid count > 100/day on a device, schedule replacement. We'll batch replacements by pod-eviction windows to avoid wide impact.
jen: creating ticket INFRA-6723 with logs, prometheus panels, and suggested runbook. linking here: https://jira.redwood/INFRA-6723 — added initial checklist and owner (jen).
kai: thumbs-up. once INFRA-6723 has the test node driver-rollback results, we can update alert thresholds and tagging so autoscaling avoids the affected nodes during peak. :thumbsup:
jen: I'll start the staging rollback and add the panels. will update this thread with results. thanks all.
ops-bot: note: next oncall rotation @sre-oncall on 2026-05-06 08:00 UTC.
